questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following :
questions.solution:
When a salt containing the acetate anion ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}$) is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) is formed.

$2\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

Acetic acid vapours are colourless and have a characteristic smell of vinegar. Being acidic in nature, these vapours turn blue litmus paper red.

Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) gives $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas which has a rotten egg smell.

Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) does not react with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) gives $\text{CO}_2$ gas which is odourless.

Answer: Acetate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}$

D. $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added to a solid nitrite salt, the gas evolved is initially colourless inside the liquid but turns into reddish-brown fumes at the mouth of the test tube.

Reason (R): Nitrite reacts with dilute acid to yield colourless nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$) gas, which is rapidly oxidized by atmospheric oxygen to form brown nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The assertion is a true factual observation from qualitative analysis. When dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added to a nitrite salt, a colourless gas is initially evolved which turns brown at the mouth of the test tube.

The reason is false. Nitrite reacts with dilute acid to yield nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), not nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$). $\text{NO}$ is a colourless gas that is rapidly oxidized by atmospheric oxygen to form brown nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$). The reactions are:
$3\text{NO}_2^- + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NO}_3^- + 2\text{NO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$ (brown fumes).

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

Match List-I with List-II concerning the preliminary tests of anions using dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

List-I (Anion)List-II (Observation)
(A) Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$)(I) Reddish-brown gas
(B) Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$)(II) Suffocating smell of burning sulphur
(C) Sulphite ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$)(III) Brisk effervescence
(D) Nitrite ($\text{NO}_2^{-}$)(IV) Rotten egg smell

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
When treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$:

Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) gives $\text{CO}_2$ gas which produces brisk effervescence.

Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) gives $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas which has a characteristic rotten egg smell.

Sulphite ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$) gives $\text{SO}_2$ gas which has a suffocating smell of burning sulphur.

Nitrite ($\text{NO}_2^{-}$) gives $\text{NO}_2$ gas which is a reddish-brown gas.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the preliminary tests of anions with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$:

I. A carbonate salt gives a colourless and odourless gas that turns lime water milky.
II. A sulphide salt evolves a gas with a pungent smell of burning sulphur.
III. A sulphite salt evolves a gas that turns acidified potassium dichromate paper green.
IV. A nitrite salt yields a colourless gas which turns into reddish-brown fumes on contact with air.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: Carbonate salts react with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to evolve $\text{CO}_2$ gas, which is colourless, odourless, and turns lime water milky.

Statement II is incorrect: Sulphide salts evolve $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas, which has a characteristic smell of rotten eggs. The pungent smell of burning sulphur is a characteristic of $\text{SO}_2$ gas (evolved from sulphites).

Statement III is correct: Sulphite salts evolve $\text{SO}_2$ gas, which is a reducing agent and turns acidified potassium dichromate paper green due to the formation of $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ions.

Statement IV is correct: Nitrite salts react with dilute acids to yield nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), which is colourless but rapidly oxidises in air to form reddish-brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$).

Therefore, three statements (I, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Addition of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to a solid nitrite salt produces a reddish-brown gas.
Reason (R) : The reaction initially produces unstable nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) which decomposes to yield nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), which is readily oxidised by air to form reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. When dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added to a nitrite ($\text{NO}_2^{-}$) salt, a reddish-brown gas is evolved.

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains (A). The reaction of nitrite with dilute acid produces nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$). Nitrous acid is unstable and disproportionates to give nitric acid, water, and nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$).

$3\text{HNO}_2 \rightarrow \text{HNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{NO}$

Nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$) is a colourless gas, but it readily reacts with atmospheric oxygen to form nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$), which is a reddish-brown gas.

$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unknown salt on heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ produces a brown gas. The evolution of this gas is significantly enhanced when copper turnings are added to the reaction mixture. Furthermore, the aqueous solution of the salt gives a brown ring at the junction of the liquids when treated with freshly prepared $\text{FeSO}_4$ solution followed by the careful addition of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ along the sides of the test tube.

Identify the anion present in the salt and the chemical formula of the brown ring complex formed.
questions.solution:
The evolution of a brown gas upon heating a salt with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, which is further intensified by the addition of copper turnings, is a characteristic confirmatory test for the nitrate ($\text{NO}_3^-$) ion. The copper turnings reduce the formed nitric acid to nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$), a brown gas.

The aqueous solution of a nitrate salt gives a positive brown ring test when treated with freshly prepared $\text{FeSO}_4$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. In this test, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces nitrate to nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), which then coordinates with the remaining $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to form the brown ring complex.

The chemical formula of the brown ring complex is $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]^{2+}$.

Answer: $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown salt on treatment with dilute $\text{HCl}$ evolves a colourless gas having a rotten egg smell. When an aqueous solution of this salt is treated with sodium nitroprusside solution, a characteristic colour is observed. Identify the colour of the resulting complex.
questions.solution:
The evolution of a colourless gas with a rotten egg smell on treatment with dilute $\text{HCl}$ indicates the presence of the sulphide anion ($\text{S}^{2-}$). The gas evolved is hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$).

As a confirmatory test, when an aqueous solution of a sulphide salt is treated with sodium nitroprusside ($\text{Na}_2[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NO}]$), a purple or violet colouration is obtained due to the formation of the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$.

$\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$ (Purple/Violet)

A black precipitate is formed in the lead acetate test for sulphide. A brown ring is the confirmatory test for nitrate. A yellow precipitate is formed in the confirmatory test for phosphate or arsenic.

Answer: Purple or violet colouration

When an aqueous solution of $X$ is treated with sodium nitroprusside solution, a purple-coloured complex $Z$ is formed. Identify the gas $Y$ and the formula of the complex $Z$.
questions.solution:
The gas $Y$ evolved with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ having a rotten egg smell is hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$). This indicates the presence of sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) ions in the salt $X$.

$\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$

Thus, the purple complex $Z$ is $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]$.

Answer: $Y = \text{H}_2\text{S}$, $Z = \text{Na}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]$

questions.q: When a solid salt is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, a colourless gas with a pungent odour is evolved. When a glass rod dipped in aqueous ammonia is brought near the mouth of the test tube, dense white fumes are observed. Identify the correct anion present in the salt :
questions.solution:
When a salt containing the chloride anion ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) gas is evolved.

$\text{Cl}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \text{HSO}_4^{-}$

$\text{HCl}$ is a colourless gas with a pungent smell. When a glass rod dipped in aqueous ammonia ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) is brought near it, dense white fumes of ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) are formed.

$\text{HCl} + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ (dense white fumes)

Bromide gives reddish-brown fumes of $\text{Br}_2$, nitrate gives brown fumes of $\text{NO}_2$, and sulphate does not react with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to evolve such gases.

Answer: Chloride, $\text{Cl}^{-}$
